title: The Deepfake Dilemma: The Technology, Policy, and Economy

reader_summary.headline: At the end of last year, there were 120 tools with which you can clone someone's voice.
reader_summary.overview: At the end of last year, there were 120 tools with which you can clone someone's voice. And by March of this year, it's become 350. Being able to identify what is real is going to become really important, especially because now you can do all of these things at scale.

thesis: The episode discusses the rapid proliferation of deepfake technology, noting that the number of voice cloning tools grew from 120 to 350 between last year and March of this year, while the cost of creation has dropped to near zero requiring only three to fifteen seconds of audio. The speakers explain that deepfakes utilize generative adversarial networks to create realistic imitations of human speech and video, making them increasingly difficult to distinguish from reality despite the existence of detection tools.
